pages: R7 historical syllabus fixture. Course 6.006, Introduction to Algorithms, was taught in Spring 2020. The course belongs to the Electrical Engineering and Computer Science department and is undergraduate level. The instructors were Erik Demaine, Jason Ku, and Justin Solomon. The meeting pattern was two one-hour lectures and two one-hour recitations each week. This concise evaluation adaptation was checked against the cited MIT OpenCourseWare syllabus on 2026-09-08 and is not a current MIT catalog statement.

Prerequisite and topic facts. Course 6.006 required 6.0001, Introduction to Computer Science and Programming in Python. Course 6.006 also required 6.042J, Mathematics for Computer Science. The course covered elementary data structures and algorithmic approaches including sorting, graph searching, and dynamic programming. Adapted from MIT OpenCourseWare under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; changes were made for a noncommercial retrieval fixture, and no MIT endorsement is implied.

pages: R7 historical syllabus fixture. Course 6.852J, Distributed Algorithms, was taught in Fall 2009. It belongs to Electrical Engineering and Computer Science and Mathematics and is graduate level. The instructor was Nancy Lynch. The course met for two ninety-minute lectures each week. It covered distributed algorithms, impossibility results, fault tolerance, and concurrent programming. This concise evaluation adaptation was checked against the cited MIT OpenCourseWare syllabus on 2026-09-08 and is not a current MIT catalog statement.

Preparation facts. Course 6.033, Computer System Engineering, was described as good background for 6.852J. Course 6.046J, Design and Analysis of Algorithms, was described as sufficient sequential-algorithms preparation. Formal-model experience was desirable but not essential; 6.045J or 18.404J/6.840J were examples. These are preparation strengths, not one flat list of mandatory prerequisites. Adapted from MIT OpenCourseWare under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; changes were made for a noncommercial retrieval fixture, and no MIT endorsement is implied.
